problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
examples.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043954/assets/966d2d7cd1cd0ef04a1d9b2adc04511dea86cbbf254166988a7072e952879fe0.png)
examples.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=13 \\ 5{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 7{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 5 & 4 & -5 \\ 7 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 14 & -70 \\ 7 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 14 & -70 \\ 0 & 16 & k-91\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{14}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 16 & k-91\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-16{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & k-11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k-11$. Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0 = k-11 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=11.
$$

feedback.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=12,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $b$ does *not* lie in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$
